note: What this decoder asserts about the S-DD1, and where each assertion comes from. No manufacturer document for this part is known to exist, so every entry names the evidence it does have and says plainly that it is not a document.

order: a manufacturer document, of which there is none
a retail cartridge, for anything a stream in one can settle
the reference decoder, for the output values, which nothing else on this machine can produce
authority.why: The S-DD1 was a Ricoh part made for Nintendo and neither published a datasheet. Everything anybody knows about the algorithm was reconstructed from the silicon or from its output, so the top rung of the ladder is empty here and the entries below say what stands in for it.
authority.whatIsMissing: A Ricoh or Nintendo datasheet for the S-DD1. Searched on 2026-08-21; nothing was found, and nothing suggests one was ever published.

comparedAgainst.what: The reference decoder, built from a pinned commit and asked to expand 4,000 streams of noise and 2,652 cartridge-shaped ones. Noise rather than artwork, because artwork walks the probability model along the path a picture happens to take and leaves most of the state table unvisited.

bitplaneCounts.why: Two bits of the header select how many bit planes a stream interleaves, and these are the four counts they select. The values are a property of the chip's interface rather than of any encoder, because an encoder takes whichever of the sixteen header shapes fits its data.
bitplaneCounts.evidence: The reference decoder, corroborated by every stream decoding to its declared length.
bitplaneCounts.howToSettleIt: A datasheet, or a die photograph of the header decode.

headerBytes.why: A stream begins with two bytes: the shape byte and one more.
headerBytes.evidence: The reference decoder, corroborated by the streams in tagged builds.

contextCount.why: How many probability contexts the arithmetic coder keeps.
contextCount.howToSettleIt: A datasheet, or a die photograph of the context memory.

maximumLength.why: A stream decodes at most one sixty four kilobyte block. This is the one figure with a second witness that is not a decoder: it is the size of a bank, and the chip decompresses into one.
maximumLength.evidence: The reference decoder, and the console's own bank size.

headerShapes.why: Four bit plane selections times four context selections.
headerShapes.evidence: Follows from the two two-bit fields above.

resetLine.value: $4800 and $4801 cleared, $4804 to $4807 set to 0, 1, 2 and 3, and every snooped channel cleared
resetLine.evidence: Two implementations agree on the registers: ares at commit 9408cb43d4948fc3ea6e152a307a34348df3fe04, ares/sfc/coprocessor/sdd1/sdd1.cpp and ares/System/Super Famicom/boards.bml, SDD1::power; and snes9x at commit 1bcc369e89f08243e0a462882fb1f3e42e51de3a, sdd1.cpp, ppu.cpp, dma.cpp and memmap.cpp, S9xResetSDD1. Only ares clears its copy of the channel registers; in snes9x that copy is the console's own DMA registers, which a reset of this chip does not touch. Construction leaves every register holding a value drawn from the seed and never calls reset. bsnes at commit 78474e5d39f58872dc21aca18cf9eb583b147fe7 carries the same file as ares with the same logic, so ares and bsnes are one witness. snes9x is a second, written separately.
resetLine.howToSettleIt: A capture of the cartridge bus across a console reset, reading $4800 to $4807 back before any write.

registerWindow.why: Where the console reaches the chip's registers.
registerWindow.evidence: One implementation: ares at commit 9408cb43d4948fc3ea6e152a307a34348df3fe04, ares/sfc/coprocessor/sdd1/sdd1.cpp and ares/System/Super Famicom/boards.bml. snes9x answers $4800 to $4807 and leaves $4808 to $480f to open bus. bsnes at commit 78474e5d39f58872dc21aca18cf9eb583b147fe7 carries the same file as ares with the same logic, so ares and bsnes are one witness. snes9x is a second, written separately.
registerWindow.howToSettleIt: A capture of the cartridge bus while a console programs the registers and runs a transfer.

value.$4800: decompression enable, one bit a DMA channel
value.$4801: decompression enable, one bit a DMA channel, cleared when that channel's transfer ends

enableRegisters.why: Two eight bit registers each name the channels allowed to decompress.
enableRegisters.evidence: Two implementations agree: ares at commit 9408cb43d4948fc3ea6e152a307a34348df3fe04, ares/sfc/coprocessor/sdd1/sdd1.cpp and ares/System/Super Famicom/boards.bml; and snes9x at commit 1bcc369e89f08243e0a462882fb1f3e42e51de3a, sdd1.cpp, ppu.cpp, dma.cpp and memmap.cpp. bsnes at commit 78474e5d39f58872dc21aca18cf9eb583b147fe7 carries the same file as ares with the same logic, so ares and bsnes are one witness. snes9x is a second, written separately.
enableRegisters.howToSettleIt: A capture of the cartridge bus while a console programs the registers and runs a transfer.

bankRegisters.why: Each register names the megabyte of ROM a sixteen bank window shows.
bankRegisters.evidence: Two implementations agree: ares at commit 9408cb43d4948fc3ea6e152a307a34348df3fe04, ares/sfc/coprocessor/sdd1/sdd1.cpp and ares/System/Super Famicom/boards.bml; and snes9x at commit 1bcc369e89f08243e0a462882fb1f3e42e51de3a, sdd1.cpp, ppu.cpp, dma.cpp and memmap.cpp. bsnes at commit 78474e5d39f58872dc21aca18cf9eb583b147fe7 carries the same file as ares with the same logic, so ares and bsnes are one witness. snes9x is a second, written separately.
bankRegisters.howToSettleIt: A capture of the cartridge bus while a console programs the registers and runs a transfer.

dmaSnoop.why: The chip watches the console write each channel's DMA registers, because it decompresses only for a read of the address a channel was given.
dmaSnoop.evidence: Two implementations agree: ares at commit 9408cb43d4948fc3ea6e152a307a34348df3fe04, ares/sfc/coprocessor/sdd1/sdd1.cpp and ares/System/Super Famicom/boards.bml; and snes9x at commit 1bcc369e89f08243e0a462882fb1f3e42e51de3a, sdd1.cpp, ppu.cpp, dma.cpp and memmap.cpp. bsnes at commit 78474e5d39f58872dc21aca18cf9eb583b147fe7 carries the same file as ares with the same logic, so ares and bsnes are one witness. snes9x is a second, written separately.
dmaSnoop.howToSettleIt: A capture of the cartridge bus while a console programs the registers and runs a transfer.

decompressionTrigger.value: a read of $c0-ff whose address equals the snooped address of a channel enabled in both $4800 and $4801
decompressionTrigger.why: What makes the chip answer with decompressed bytes rather than ROM.
decompressionTrigger.evidence: One implementation: ares at commit 9408cb43d4948fc3ea6e152a307a34348df3fe04, ares/sfc/coprocessor/sdd1/sdd1.cpp and ares/System/Super Famicom/boards.bml. snes9x tests only $4801, and only when a DMA with a fixed A-bus address starts. bsnes at commit 78474e5d39f58872dc21aca18cf9eb583b147fe7 carries the same file as ares with the same logic, so ares and bsnes are one witness. snes9x is a second, written separately.
decompressionTrigger.howToSettleIt: A capture of the cartridge bus while a console programs the registers and runs a transfer.

transferEnd.value: after the snooped count of bytes, a count of 0 meaning 65,536, the channel's $4801 bit clears and the next read starts a new stream
transferEnd.evidence: Two implementations agree: ares at commit 9408cb43d4948fc3ea6e152a307a34348df3fe04, ares/sfc/coprocessor/sdd1/sdd1.cpp and ares/System/Super Famicom/boards.bml; and snes9x at commit 1bcc369e89f08243e0a462882fb1f3e42e51de3a, sdd1.cpp, ppu.cpp, dma.cpp and memmap.cpp. bsnes at commit 78474e5d39f58872dc21aca18cf9eb583b147fe7 carries the same file as ares with the same logic, so ares and bsnes are one witness. snes9x is a second, written separately.
transferEnd.howToSettleIt: A capture of the cartridge bus while a console programs the registers and runs a transfer.

programWindow.why: How the console reaches the program in ROM.
programWindow.evidence: One implementation: ares at commit 9408cb43d4948fc3ea6e152a307a34348df3fe04, ares/sfc/coprocessor/sdd1/sdd1.cpp and ares/System/Super Famicom/boards.bml. snes9x maps it the same way and has no fold; ares folds banks $20-3f onto $00-1f when bit 7 of $4805 is set, and $a0-bf onto $80-9f when bit 7 of $4807 is set. bsnes at commit 78474e5d39f58872dc21aca18cf9eb583b147fe7 carries the same file as ares with the same logic, so ares and bsnes are one witness. snes9x is a second, written separately.
programWindow.howToSettleIt: A capture of the cartridge bus while a console programs the registers and runs a transfer.

notStated: Everything. No manufacturer document for this part is known to exist, so nothing here is verified in the sense the sibling repositories use the word.
How the chip behaves on a malformed stream. Every implementation guesses, and none of the guesses can be checked.
Anything about timing. How long the chip takes to decode a block, and whether the console can outrun it, is unmodelled and unmeasured.
What the second header byte means beyond selecting a shape.
What a read past the end of the ROM returns. Neither implementation defines it; this package repeats the ROM.
Whether a read of an armed address that is not part of a DMA transfer decompresses. ares says it does; snes9x decompresses only inside a transfer.
